correction: I had described publishing the engine global as something the host does afterwards. The body shows it is a prerequisite: Engine::Initialize itself reads that global partway through.

evidence.0x18007471f: mov rcx,[0x180421428] - Initialize reads the engine global from inside its own body
evidence.0x180074726: call 0x180073660 - obtains an object from that global
evidence.0x18007472b to 0x180074735: Options::GetString is invoked on it, producing a string at [rbp-0x20]
evidence.0x18007473b to 0x180074754: that string is then passed into a call through [rax] before the GraphicsEngine allocation, so the value is consumed early

consequence: A host must store its Engine object pointer into Engine.dll+0x421428 before calling Engine::Initialize, otherwise the function dereferences null at 0x18007471f.
why_this_matters: This also means the game cannot be starting the engine in the order I assumed. The game must publish the pointer first and call Initialize afterwards, which is consistent with a factory or accessor pattern rather than with Initialize publishing itself.
revised_host_sequence: load Engine.dll and resolve the exports
construct WinWindow and call Initialize to obtain a real EWindow
allocate the Engine buffer (at least 0xC28 bytes) and call Engine::Engine()
store the Engine pointer into Engine.dll+0x421428 - this is the publish step and it must happen before the next step
call Engine::Initialize(window, settings, bool, FileSystem*, string, bool, string, string, string, string)
not_established: what 0x180073660 returns and whether it tolerates a partially initialised Engine
whether Options::GetString succeeds when no Options object exists
whether the string it produces must name a real file
